classification.label_note: Bands are the dataset's own terciles of price per sq.ft. Because the label is derived from the target, this is a discretised view of the regression problem, not independent information.
classification.split: GroupShuffleSplit by locality/ward — no locality spans the split
classification.warning: DEGENERATE MODEL — the classifier never predicts Mid-market. It has collapsed toward a single class, so its accuracy of 0.366 is not evidence that it works. With only 7 spatial group(s), holding out whole localities leaves the model no basis for placing an area it has never seen. This result should be reported as a failure to generalise, not as a model.

clustering.reason: Only 7 localities have 5+ records — too few to cluster meaningfully.

lof.defines_unusual_as: lower local density than its neighbours

dbscan.defines_unusual_as: not density-reachable from a core point
dbscan.eps_note: DBSCAN has no contamination parameter. eps is the 95% quantile of the distance to the 5th nearest neighbour, so all three detectors work to the same budget and the comparison is about which rows, not how many.

anomaly.agreement_note: Three detectors, one feature matrix, one 5% budget. Jaccard is used because agreement on the ~95% of rows nobody flagged is not informative. Rows all three flag are unusual under three different definitions; rows only one flags say more about that detector than about the property.
anomaly.note: Flags records that are unusual across their whole feature vector, which is a different question from the price-interval check: that asks whether a price is far from the model, this asks whether the record itself is atypical.
anomaly.caveat: An anomaly is not evidence of anything wrong. Contamination is set at 5% by assumption, so roughly 5% of records will be flagged whatever the data looks like.
